target_paper.title: Accuracy and Political Bias of News Source Credibility Ratings by Large Language Models
target_paper.original_source: released llm_ratings.parquet re-scored (Figure 3 rho 0.54/0.62, 41.2% unrated, Figure 6 no significant default liberal bias)

generation.parameters: temperature 0, response_format json_object, system SYS_BASE + user instruction/format (code/query_llm.py, prompt_factory.py)

political_original.note: left/right = sign of the Robertson score (paper's exact split not in the repo); liberal bias = higher LLM-minus-expert on left sources

political_reexecution.note: left/right = sign of the Robertson score (paper's exact split not in the repo); liberal bias = higher LLM-minus-expert on left sources

results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN §1; human double-coding pending
results.note: Accuracy half survives exactly (rho 0.629 vs 0.624 own; 0.544 vs 0.537 common set; per-domain agreement rho 0.974, mean |diff| 0.011). The refusal share fell from 0.412 to 0.354 (7.0% of domains changed rated/unrated status). The political-bias half changes qualitatively: left-minus-right rating bias +0.012 (was +0.008) with Welch p = 0.045 (was 0.161), so the paper's 'no significant liberal bias for GPT-4 Turbo' statement no longer holds at alpha 0.05 under our left/right split (sign of the Robertson score; the paper's exact split is not in the repository).
